question: How are NYC crashes distributed across the days of the week, 2013 to 2025?

options.metric: Total number of police-reported crash records in 2013–2025 by weekday
options.denominator: No denominator; each row is one crash record
options.grouping: Weekday derived from crash_date, Monday through Sunday
options.reason: A total-count view directly shows how the crash records in the requested period are distributed among weekdays.
options.answer: Of the 2,132,218 police-reported crashes dated 2013–2025, Friday had the most records (338,800) and Sunday the fewest (257,544).
options.interpretation: This framing answers the weekday distribution as total crash-record counts: Friday has the most (338,800) and Sunday the fewest (257,544) among 2,132,218 records dated 2013–2025. It is defensible because each row represents one police-reported crash and the requested period is pooled into weekday groups. It does not normalize for how many dates of each weekday occur or measure crashes per trip, person, or traffic volume. The check found 0 missing dates and 0 checked sentinel dates among 2,269,187 source rows; it excludes 136,969 dated rows outside 2013–2025 and keeps all 2,132,218 in-scope rows, with each year's observed date envelope reaching both boundaries although daily completeness is unverified.

options.denominator: Number of calendar dates of that weekday in the inclusive span: Monday 678; Tuesday 679; Wednesday 679; Thursday 678; Friday 678; Saturday 678; Sunday 678

options.answer: The mean was highest on Fridays at 499.7 crash records per Friday date and lowest on Sundays at 379.9 per Sunday date over 2013–2025.
